A.title: Home fees for EU students, but capped, reciprocal and costed in public
A.answer: Keep the current fee system and universities; change the terms of the tuition deal due within six months (s4). Home-rate fees apply to EU students only inside a fixed yearly cap on places, set by ministers and kept separate from places for UK students, so none are cut. The deal starts only when the EU gives UK students equal fees. The Treasury publishes the yearly gap and funds it from a named budget line, not from NHS or school money. Parliament reviews it after three years, and the cap shrinks or the deal ends if the gap passes the published limit. It worked if UK places hold, the gap stays inside the limit, and UK students use the reciprocal rate. Universities warn that cuts would squeeze places (s4).

B.title: A joint fees board, not a trade-off behind closed doors
B.answer: Take the fee question out of the wider trade talks and give it to a joint UK-EU fees board with equal seats for UK students, EU students and universities, plus a fixed budget. The two governments would set that up within weeks, inside the six months they have already agreed for a fees deal (s4). EU officials say the deal hangs on fees, and the UK disputes that (s4), so a separate board lets the food, carbon and youth parts go ahead. Universities warn that any fee cut would squeeze UK places (s4), and 26 simulated citizens set a limit of no free places paid by taxpayers, so the board's pot must be named and capped. It worked if the rest of the deal is not held up, the fee rate is published, and UK places do not fall.
